question_en: Which automatic weather station was photographed in this image?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 2-2-E03

## Step 01 · Record weather station structure, enter historical photo archive

**Action:** Observe the automatic weather station in the snow. Use search queries like "Greenland automatic weather station two booms historical photos" to find historical archives containing station names, then enter the Historical GC-Net AWS photo archive.

**Evidence Observation:** The wind sensors on the horizontal booms at both levels extend to the left side of the image; the middle-upper part of the mast has two dark solar panels, a horizontal multi-rod antenna, and a white box, with cable coils visible below; a snowmobile is in the lower right, and mountains are in the distant right background. The person is pixelated; do not use clothing or actions for judgment. Generic towers can only provide search direction; the station name must be given by the corresponding photo record.

Archive page and record metadata:
https://zenodo.org/records/8307936

https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936

## Step 02 · Locate photo from ZIP directory, verify composition point by point

**Action:** First use the archive ZIP's directory preview and container interface to find the image; there is no need to download the entire compressed package to view a single photo. View the photo named "JR2 2003 04 27a K Steffen.jpg" in the JAR2 directory.

Directory preview and API for expandable directories:
https://zenodo.org/records/8307936/preview/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip

https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/container

Direct link to target photo:
https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/container/all_pictures_GC-Net/JAR2/JR2%202003%2004%2027a%20K%20Steffen.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** The wind instruments on two layers extending to the left, the relative positions of solar panels, antenna, white box, and cable coils in the target photo, as well as the snowmobile in the lower right and the mountain shape on the right, all align with the input. The directory uses JAR2, while the filename uses the abbreviation JR2; the abbreviation is not a different station.

**Result of this step:** The archive attribution for the same image has been found; its directory information can support the station name, and one cannot guess based solely on similar appearance.

## Step 03 · Make limited comparison with similar GC-Net towers

**Action:** Check the photos of JAR3, CP2, and Petermann ELA in the question package, which are most easily confused, to judge based on relative component positions and shared environment.

- In JAR3's 2003 photo, the wind instrument boom faces right, the single solar panel is higher, the white box is on the left, and the snow surface texture is different.
- In CP2's 1998 photo, the wind instrument extends to the right, the solar panel is mounted vertically at the top, the box is close to the snow surface, and the mast and guy-wire layout are different.
- Although Petermann ELA also has a left-extending boom, it has back-to-back dual panels, a vertical thin antenna, a lower box, and a different cable layout; one cannot identify it as the image in the question based solely on the boom direction.

JAR3 reference photo:
https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/container/all_pictures_GC-Net/JAR3/JR3%202003%2006%2003pre%20K%20Steffen.jpg

CP2 reference photo:
https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/container/all_pictures_GC-Net/CP2%201998%20PRE%20J%20Box.jpg

Petermann ELA reference photo:
https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/container/all_pictures_GC-Net/Petermann%20ELA/PET%202018%20via%20D%20Houtz.JPG

**Result of this step:** Towers within the same project are not identical; the complete component combination and original photo correspondence support JAR2.

## Step 04 · Standardize station name, retain traceable attachments, then stop

**Action:** Verify the formal station name JAR2 against the station list in the GC-Net paper to avoid treating the photo filename JR2 directly as the final name.

Paper and station list image:
https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/15/5467/2023/essd-15-5467-2023.html

https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/15/5467/2023/essd-15-5467-2023-t01.png

Complete photo ZIP attachment and JAR2 directory, which can be used for subsequent review of other views of the same station; this is not another independent measurement:
https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/content

https://zenodo.org/api/records/8307936/files/historical_GC-Net_photos.zip/container/all_pictures_GC-Net/JAR2

The question package also retains 2003 annual materials; the cover involves JAR3 and cannot be used to name this image based on that cover:
https://polardata.ch/PDFs/SteK_Steffen%2C%20Konrad%2C%202003%2C%20M%C3%A4rz.pdf

**Stopping condition:** The same-image match, archive directory, and formal station name have been correlated; the question only asks for the station name, so output JAR2.

## Formal Answer

JAR2
